headline: Canadian Nickel Mine to Capture 1.5M Tons of Carbon Yearly
meta_description: Canada Nickel Company receives final approval for Crawford Project, a nickel mine that will capture and store 1.5 million tons of CO2 annually using breakthrou…
summary_short: Ontario approves Canada's largest nickel mine, which will capture carbon at unprecedented scale—equivalent to removing 350,000 cars from roads yearly.
body:
Canada Nickel Company has received final permitting approval from the Ontario government for its Crawford Project, marking a historic milestone for responsible resource extraction. The mine, located in Ontario's Timmins mining district, will produce nickel from an estimated 3.8 million-ton deposit while simultaneously capturing and storing atmospheric carbon at an industrial scale—approximately 1.5 million tons of CO2 per year during operations. This carbon-capture feat equals the emissions prevented by removing 350,000 gas-powered vehicles from roads annually. The approval came under Canada's reformed Impact Assessment Act, designed to fast-track high-quality extractive projects, and represents the first permit issued under these new regulations.

What sets Crawford apart is its proprietary In-Process Tailings Carbonization technology, which injects concentrated CO2 directly into mining waste while it remains in the processing circuit. Lab tests show this method captures carbon 8 to 12 times faster than passive approaches, reaching net-zero targets in under 36 hours. The company will fund part of the $1.9 billion project through carbon credit sales, potentially claiming up to 50% in tax credits for carbon storage incentives.

The Crawford Project addresses a critical global supply chain problem. Indonesia currently controls 67% of world nickel production—more market dominance than OPEC holds over oil—while nickel mining has become a primary driver of deforestation on Indonesian islands like Sulawesi and Halmahera. Western manufacturers have long lacked alternative sources, forcing them to source from regions where environmental oversight remains limited. Canada Nickel aims to establish the world's largest Western-accessible nickel mine operated under rigorous environmental standards. With a projected 41-year operational life, the company estimates carbon storage potential could eventually reach 15 million tons annually—a generational opportunity to remove greenhouse gases while meeting critical demand for stainless steel, plating, and next-generation electric vehicle batteries.
quick_facts: Ontario approves Crawford Project, first permit under reformed Impact Assessment Act
Mine will capture and store 1.5 million tons of CO2 annually during operation
Located in Timmins mining district; contains estimated 3.8 million tons of nickel
Project requires $1.9 billion investment; construction decision targeted for 2027
Carbon capture is 8-12 times faster than passive methods, achieving targets in under 36 hours
